segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמְקַבֵּל שָׂדֶה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ וְהִיא בֵּית הַשְּׁלָחִין, אוֹ בֵּית הָאִילָן, יָבַשׁ הַמַּעְיָן וְנִקְצַץ הָאִילָן – אֵינוֹ מְנַכֶּה לוֹ מִן חֲכוֹרוֹ. אִם אָמַר לוֹ: ״חֲכוֹר לִי שָׂדֶה בֵּית הַשְּׁלָחִין זוֹ״ אוֹ ״שְׂדֵה בֵּית הָאִילָן זֶה״, יָבַשׁ הַמַּעְיָן וְנִקְצַץ הָאִילָן – מְנַכֶּה לוֹ מֵחֲכוֹרוֹ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «one who receives a field from another» to cultivate «and it is an irrigated» field «or a field with trees,» if «the spring» that irrigated the field «dried up or the trees were cut down,» he does «not subtract from» the produce «he» owes the owner as part of «his tenancy,» despite the fact that he presumably considered these factors when agreeing to cultivate the field. But «if» the cultivator «said to» the landowner explicitly: «Lease me this irrigated field, or» he said: Lease me «this field with trees,» and «the spring dried up or the trees were cut down, he» may «subtract from» the produce «he» owes as part of «his tenancy.»
